Variants.Content: Lone Light Castle is located on Lone Light Island, the most remote island in the Iron Islands. It is the seat of a branch of House Harlaw. The weight of distance is felt even more on islands far from Pike: supply ships are late, messengers are blocked by storms, and lights are both a guide and a solitude on the night sea. The people of Gudeng Island still share the culture of the Drowned God, longships, and salt winds with the islands, but because of their remoteness, they value books, trade, and access to outside information even more. The lighthouse of the fortress or the light of the fire on the top can identify the direction of the ships familiar with the waterway, and also remind visitors that this is not a deserted place.

Entry Lonely Light Local families also relied on salt fish, ore, barren fields, sheltered anchorages, and longships to return home; if any road, well, or dock failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Lonely Light If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

From workshops to sanctuaries, Gudeng Castle juxtaposes boats, bridges, millstones, fishing nets and riverside churches with the Drowned God, sea stones and songs left by the island's ancestors. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Lonely Light They care about salt fish, ore, barren fields, sheltered anchorages, and the return of longships. They also look at whether seeds are left after collecting grain and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
